entities.summary: Michael Derek Elworthy Jarman was an English artist, film maker, stage designer, writer, gardener, and gay rights activist, regarded as one of the most influential figures associated with the new queer cinema. Trained originally as a painter, he moved into stage and production design in the late 1960s, including work on Ken Russell's controversial historical 1971 film The Devils, before turning to filmmaking as a director. Derek Jarman was a authors & novelists from Northwood (1942-01-31, Northwood–1994-02-19). A moderately significant entity in the historical record. Relevant to cause-and-effect analysis.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a key figure in the new queer cinema, Derek Jarman's work influenced LGBTQ+ representation and visibility in film. His innovative filmmaking style and activism contributed to the development of queer cinema as a distinct genre.
